# WIRE coordination

Keep useful work moving toward a coherent, working WIRE experience. A small
outcome is an independently demonstrable result, not a tiny permission to proceed.

## 1. Recover the current job

Establish the user's requested outcome, applicable decisions, actual owners,
accepted input and remaining acceptance gap. Reuse an existing current record;
read further only to resolve a specific missing or contradictory fact.

Treat direct user decisions as distinct from proposals, relays and historical
instructions. Reconcile repository and accepted local work when relevant;
an older handoff or default branch can lag accepted work. Keep operational paths,
private feedback and grants in private task records, not repository skills or
published source.

For successor preparation, activation or worker replacement, read
[takeover](references/takeover.md) before changing ownership.
Reading this skill alone neither appoints a coordinator nor grants operations.

**Ready:** the outcome, responsible owner, actual authority and next action are
known, or one precise missing fact is identified.

## 2. Assign an outcome, not a sequence of approvals

Prefer the existing capable owner through diagnosis, implementation, related
documentation, focused proof and review corrections. Create fresh workers only
within the user's delegated scope and the host's actual permissions, for a
distinct outcome or context replacement. Without delegation tools or authority,
keep the work with its existing owner rather than inventing a worker hierarchy.
Respect applicable model, placement and mode choices; report unexposed settings
honestly rather than promising them through prompt text.

Put these items in the existing assignment, without a separate planning document:

- The observable user outcome and qualified source input.
- Ownership, relevant exclusions and real permission/resource boundaries.
- Concrete producer/consumer dependencies and integration owner.
- Acceptance criteria, relevant skills and the smallest meaningful proof.
- The next action after handoff; routine corrections remain within the brief.

Children need standalone context, including original feedback and attachments
when relevant and authorized. Transfer the underlying principle across affected
surfaces, not just a screenshot treatment or a command to load a skill.

Use [end-to-end delivery](../wire-end-to-end-delivery/SKILL.md) for implementation
and delivery; use [UX finish](../wire-ux-finish/SKILL.md) for affected interface
acceptance. Load only their relevant branches. A single-owner fix does not
require a multi-agent organization.

**Ready:** the owner can finish ordinary engineering without another assignment
for every lookup, edit, failed local check or correction.

## 3. Build in parallel

When coordinating a combined release, reuse or establish one authorized build
owner for composition, qualification and delivery. Keep that owner focused on
the agreed build; feature owners retain their feature corrections.

The build owner follows
[build delivery](../wire-end-to-end-delivery/references/build-delivery.md).
Supply admitted inputs, combined scope and actual standing update authority.
The coordinator continues reviews, decisions and independent work while the
batch builds.

Serialize only real conflicts: overlapping integration hunks, the same live
writer/process, same-runtime checks versus restart, source/profile custody,
or a concrete producer prerequisite. A build failure or unrelated unfinished
feature is not a global hold. Record each hold's release condition and next actor;
release it when satisfied.

**Ready:** each ready outcome is moving, and every blocked outcome has a concrete
dependency rather than a general "waiting for the build."

## 4. Coordinate by exception

Owners complete routine work autonomously within their scope. They contact the
coordinator for a reviewable result, unresolved blocker, consequential risk,
cross-owner conflict or genuinely new permission/scope decision.

Keep intermediate logs, hashes and test detail in the task record. A useful
message names the affected outcome, material change or decision, recommended
next actor and one evidence pointer. Reply only when it changes the next action.
Use completion events instead of polling or acknowledgment chains.

If chatter grows, repair assignment granularity and approval demands. Do not
merely shorten messages or interrupt a safe operation. Side questions do not
pause independent authorized work. If nothing can proceed, wait honestly.

## Completion

Inspect the composed user experience when delivery is in scope, not only
individual worker receipts. Use the applicable delivery and UX criteria without
commissioning a new review team or broad campaign by default. Keep one current
handoff distinguishing implemented, accepted, published and running work.

Report the owned outcome and its real limits, or the exact unresolved gap and
next action. A missing criterion remains unfinished even when components pass.
